lessons.title: Read for the gist
lessons.tip: The gist is the big idea of a text: what it is mostly about. Before you look for small facts, read the whole text once, quickly, and ask, “What is this about?” Do not stop for every new word.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)
Plain-language reading practice conventions (gist, detail, scanning); texts written for this app

lessons.title: Find the detail
lessons.tip: A detail is one small fact: a name, a place, a time, a reason. Read the question first. Then read the text again and look for the words that answer it. Question words such as who, when and where tell you what kind of detail to find.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)

lessons.title: Scan for facts
lessons.tip: To scan, move your eyes over the text and look for only one thing, such as a number, a name or a day. You do not read every word. Look for capital letters (names), digits (numbers) and special words like Monday.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)

lessons.title: Listen for key words
lessons.tip: When you listen, you cannot go back, so listen for the key words: the important names, numbers, places and actions. Little words like “the” and “a” are quiet and quick. Ask yourself: who is speaking, what do they want, and when or where?
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)

lessons.title: Find the main idea
lessons.tip: The main idea is the one most important point of a text. The details support it. To find it, look at the first sentence, the last sentence, and the idea that most sentences are about.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)

lessons.title: Guess meaning from context
lessons.tip: When you meet a new word, do not stop. Look at the words around it. They often give a clue: a similar word, an opposite word, or an example. Then guess the meaning and check that the sentence still makes sense.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)

lessons.title: Signal words
lessons.tip: Small words join ideas and tell you what comes next. “And” adds, “but” shows a difference, “because” gives a reason, and “so” gives a result. Notice them when you read or listen.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)

lessons.title: Fact or opinion?
lessons.tip: A fact can be checked: it is true or false. An opinion says what someone thinks or feels, and people can disagree. Words such as “I think”, “best”, “beautiful” and “should” often signal an opinion.
sources: CEFR Companion Volume (reading and listening descriptors, A1-A2)
